detail: Passivates at 93-98% H2SO4, forming a protective coating that makes concentrated acid LESS corrosive to carbon steel than dilute acid -- the standard, economical bulk-storage material at this concentration band, not a fallback.

material: Generic XLPE (rotomolded, no named vendor spec)
detail: ProTank: fails within 6 months of service at 98%. Never quote a generic catalog XLPE tank at this concentration.

service_context: Concentrated sulfuric acid, under 11,000 gal and under 15 ft tall
material: XLPE + OR-1000 antioxidant surface (Poly Processing named product)
verdict: Recommended within the stated size ceiling
detail: Poly Processing's own published "11/15 rule": any Poly Processing tank under 11,000 gallons and under 15 feet tall is fine for sulfuric acid storage. SAFE-Tank if no secondary containment exists, IMFO if it does.

material: HDLPE resin #880046 (Snyder named product, linear polyethylene, not crosslinked)
detail: A genuinely different polymer from XLPE -- Snyder's spec and ProTank's XLPE warning are not actually in conflict; they describe different materials. Built to ASTM D1998, SG to 1.9.

material: Extrusion-wound HDPE/PP, walls to 6 inches (Houston PolyTank named product)
detail: No molded-in stresses (the actual XLPE failure mechanism), engineered to German DVS 2205 standard. Vendor names sulfuric acid explicitly as a service it handles.
FRP tops out around 80% H2SO4; no public resin/concentration chart exists above that -- resin selection above 80% must be engineered per-project with the vendor, not assumed from a catalog.

verdict: Recommended up to 95%, Not Recommended above 98.3%
detail: At 98.3%+ concentration, sulfuric acid carries a natural sulfur trioxide (SO3) contaminant that attacks and stress-fractures PVDF.

verdict: Recommended up to 95%, Not Recommended above 98.3%
detail: Same SO3 attack mechanism as PVDF above 98.3%.

service_context: Concentrated sulfuric acid piping and valves
detail: Independently confirmed by a second vendor: Asahi/America's own South Florida RO plant case study specified Ultra Proline (ECTFE/Halar) + DuoPro for sulfuric acid specifically while every other chemical on the job used standard Chem Proline PE.

service_context: Concentrated sulfuric acid piping and valves
verdict: Recommended if flanged; Not Recommended if threaded
detail: Threaded PTFE fails by cold-flow leakage at the joint, not chemical attack -- a mechanical failure mode, not a chemistry one.

service_context: Concentrated sulfuric acid piping, valves, and pumps
verdict: Recommended -- most robust and most expensive option
detail: Real documented case study: a Chilean copper mine and other real installs use Alloy 20 wetted parts for concentrated sulfuric acid transfer. Not a standard catalog SKU for most pump vendors -- factor real lead time into any quote.
vendor_source: Griffco Valve; Carver Pump case study

service_context: Heap-leach control valve diaphragm (75/90/100 Series MIN configuration)
detail: Hard limit even when the valve body/liner material handles the chemical fine at higher temperature -- the diaphragm elastomer is the limiting material, not the body. Always verify operating temperature against the diaphragm rating specifically.

verdict: Not Recommended at any tested concentration
detail: Rated flatly Not Good even at 10% nitric acid.
Netafim's own catalog identifies the fix: order the valve with Hastelloy wetted components instead, explicitly because Hastelloy resists chlorine gas, hypochlorite, and chlorine dioxide solutions.
Real, named dual-chemistry rating -- the same skid family is rated for both major heap-leaching chemistries (copper SX/EW raffinate and gold/silver cyanide).
vendor_source: Netafim Mining Products catalog (Leaching Control Skid)

detail: Rated to 110 F for raffinate service specifically.
vendor_source: Netafim Mining Products catalog (Leaching Control Skid)

detail: Centrifugal pumps fail via seal degradation in abrasive slurry service, regardless of wetted material.
Seal-less, self-priming, runs dry, removes the failure mode that kills centrifugal pumps in this duty.

material: Peristaltic / hose pump (Graco SoloTech or ProMinent DULCOFLEX), CSM/Hypalon hose
detail: Hose-only wetted path -- no check valves, seals, or glands in the fluid path -- the correct architecture for abrasive, solids-bearing streams. Two independent roster vendors now confirm this architecture.
Beveled, polished/lapped gate specifically engineered to cut through solids and seal tighter when closed. Meets MSS-SP-81 and TAPPI TIS 405-8.

verdict: Recommended for light slurry only, Not Recommended for heavy slurry
detail: Explicitly NOT a general heavy-slurry pump despite sharing the Schurco family name -- a real design/duty mismatch if misapplied.

service_context: Combined corrosive + abrasive leach-circuit brine slurry
detail: Seamless-cast fiberglass/ceramic/vinyl ester matrix engineered for the case where a fluid is simultaneously corrosive AND abrasive -- PVDF solves corrosion, not abrasion; hardened alloys solve abrasion, not broad chemical resistance.
